about: Every dimension the F/A-18C build uses, with its source (an id in references.json) and where in it. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts. Stations (FS) are inches aft of the fuselage datum, waterlines (WL) inches above it (WL 100 is the fuselage reference line), buttlines (BL) inches from the centreline, positive to starboard. Angles round the fuselage (theta) follow TM-101724 figure 3: looking aft, 0 is the bottom centreline, 180 the top, 90 starboard and 270 port. A fact taken from the old model, as a last resort, names the old model as its source and says why no other source had it; a detail copied from it under the fair-use policy is listed in its manifest entry (air-fa18c.md #2).

length.also: hatp figure 2 (56.00 ft); tp209033 figure 2 (56.0 ft)
length.note: checked to the foot NATOPS gives it in (+-6 in; user, 2026-11-02): with the stabilator tips' 13 in corner rounds where the photos put them (layout.stabilator, layout.stabilator_corner) the model measures 55.76 ft, and the photos' own apex (FS 59.7, 18 photos) and aftmost point (FS 729.8) give 55.84 ft

folded.note: 27 ft 6 in. Checked over the folded panels without the fairings under them (layout.wing_fairing, NATOPS 2.6.1.2's position lights 'under the wing at the wingfold hinge'), which ride the outer panel 9 in outboard of the fold line and turn outboard with it, 4.3 in a side: with them the build spans 337.7 in folded. Photos of folded jets (2026-11-07 sweep: f6790603882, f3315245532, f15612089546, the USS Midway Museum's F/A-18A) show each fairing standing out from the folded panel's outboard face just above the hinge, its lens at its front: they fold with the panel, and NATOPS's figure leaves them out. The two folded photos solved (c8355477, c8183843) read the folded panels 2.3-5.6 in outside the build over FS 480-576 (layout.fold: the angle unsettled)

full.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

limits.about: Mechanical position and rate limits, deg and deg/s, from tp209033 table 2 (PDF page 16), which states they are the basic F-18A/B's. tm110216 table 6.2 (PDF page 99) gives the HARV's aileron as 25 up and 42 down.

waterline.note: the fuselage reference line corresponds to WL 100.0 on the airplane

buttline.note: BL 0 is the centreline; BL grows to starboard (Y is right of the c.g.)

apex.note: the fuselage reference line (WL 100) is drawn through the nose apex and on aft past the stabilator; tp209033 figure 2 points WL 100 at the stabilator

chord.note: mean aerodynamic chord, projected; tp209033 and hatp give 11.52 ft (138.24 in) as the reference chord

root.note: NACA 65A with a sharp leading edge, at wing station 56.876 (cr201687 table 1: modified NACA 65A, 5.0%)

tip.note: cr201687 table 1 agrees (3.5%); secondary sources' 65A003 is not supported

span.note: span station of the wingtip at the launcher rail, on a sketch; the reference semispan is 224.5 in

lef.note: each inboard leading-edge flap is 36.5% of the total LEF area, each outboard 13.5%; one actuator drives both

areas.note: totals for both sides. cr3608's 1/10-scale model gives 0.19, 0.55 and 0.62 ft2, which scale to 19, 55 and 62. The flaps' 48.4 is not built: their fronts stand on the hinge line the photos show (layout.hinge), which makes them 55.5

exposed.note: reference span of the exposed panels

area.note: theoretical exposed, both sides; tm4772 table 1 gives 88.26 unmodified

toe.note: toe out, as the model table gives it

top.note: the fin tip 11.34 in above the fuselage reference line on the 1/10-scale model. Anchored at the apex, the HATP side view draws it about 4 in higher and its canopy top at WL 163, which this figure also draws

forebody.note: the McDonnell Douglas drawing's forebody height and width, read off the graphs to about 1 in; agrees with tm101724's sections

buttline.note: TLOC: each engine axis 2.33 ft either side of the centreline at the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56), where the figure draws it

angle.note: EPS: the engine axis's angle to the aircraft's x axis in plan. The axes converge aft: hatp figure 2's top view draws the nozzles at BL 19.5 either side, nearly touching, as photo dvids9820758 shows, which 2 deg of convergence from 28 in at FS 458.56 gives (19.3 in at FS 707)

thrust.note: DXTHRS: the thrust point's distance aft of the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56)

inlet.note: hydraulic diameter of the inlet duct entrance

canopy.note: how much bigger the two-seat canopy is than the single-seat one; tp209033 figure 2 draws the two-seat jet

gravity.aircraft: HARV phase 1, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
HARV phases 2-3, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
F-18B SRA, 66% fuel, clean, gear up

airfoils.note: NACA 65A basic thickness forms: half-thickness y at chordwise station x, both in percent of chord. Another thickness takes y/t interpolated linearly in t between the tabulated forms (TR-84's own method, by its cross plots); above 5% the 5% ratios hold, which TR-84's 63-series cross plots show moving under 2% between 5% and 6%.

layout.about: Placements no source states, fitted to the NASA three-views with the published planforms (views.py's masks, the side view anchored at the apex on WL 100). Each says what it was fitted to. The photo gate checks them against the reference airframe's photos (photos.json).

wing.where: figure 5, PDF page 31 (traced by views.py), with hatp figure 2's side view for the keel. The anhedral: photos.py's cameras and tips.py (rotating the wing about the junction; deflections fitted, or held at rest in flight) over the ground photo dvids9820799 and the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145, their cameras solved with the rest (fin tips within 0.3 in)
wing.note: the wing's chord plane at the LEX-wing junction (BL 54.5, FS 404.05): the FS 357 section's LEX tip stands 31 in above its keel, and the keel is at WL 82.5. The anhedral is the photos', the jet parked (the user's choice, 2026-10-30): cr201687's -3 deg (wing.dihedral) leaves the tips' trailing corners about 5 in low in the ground photo (+-2 in or more: its flaps and ailerons droop) and 10 in low in three in-flight photos (8.7-10.3 leaving each out), the difference the wing bending up at 1 g (task: wing flex). Rotating the wing about the junction fits the flight photos a little better than raising it, and the junction itself measures no higher (4 in lower, +-2.3, two photos). The HATP front view draws the outer wing about 10 in higher

flex.unit: BL in, where the bend starts; in, the wingtip's rise at 1 g of lift; [BL in, share of the tip's rise]
flex.where: the rise: tm212871 printed page 17 and figure 12(a), FDMS target 12 (span station 193.8, figure 5) about 1.4 in, and 1.7 in after a roll, in steady level flight against ground rest, taken to the tip by the ground test's shape; the shape: tm210726 figure 16, load case D3, the forward box's measured deflection (1.1, 1.8, 3.1, 5.1, 6.2 and 10.0 in at the stations, 13.6 in at span station 222.1), read off the figure
flex.note: the wing bent up by lift (task: wing flex), as the shape key flex and the bend joints flex_* driven by the load factor of the lift (the drive load: 0 parked, 1 in level flight). Both reports fly the Active Aeroelastic Wing jet, whose wing has the preproduction torsional stiffness, a little softer than a production C's; its targets outboard of the fold carry the fold's free play. The bend starts at the LEX-wing junction (layout.wing's buttline) and takes a cantilever's shape, lift along the span as the chord and stiffness as the chord times the section's depth squared, streamwise sections rigid: outboard of BL 150 it follows the ground test's shape within 0.015 of the tip's rise, inboard it bends 0.05-0.06 less (the test's load and the fuselage's restraint are not flight's). The photo match agrees within its uncertainty: posed at 1 g with the in-flight photos, the wingtips' trailing corners fit best near a 3.5 in rise and the parked photos' wing and fin edges best with none

fold.unit: deg, the outer wing's turn about the fold line from spread
fold.where: the two photos with the wings folded against the sky (c8355477, deck level ahead of the right wing; c8183843, head-on): c8355477's outline fits best at 103 deg and its tip corners at 101, c8183843's corners at 95-99 (its outline keeps too few of its places as the angle changes to settle one); the middle of those readings
fold.note: NATOPS's folded span (27 ft 6 in) holds at any angle past 90 deg, where the panel's foot at the fold line stands outermost, so it cannot fix the angle: the build took the least angle that met it, 90.1 deg. At 98 deg the two photos still read the folded panel inside their outlines, 2.3-5.6 in (painted49), and pull opposite ways: c8355477's fits best at 103, c8183843's places thin out past 94 and read 0 at 83-92. No one angle fits both, so the panel's own shape or the fold line's place is unsettled, not only its angle. Two more folded views (2026-11-08: f3315245532 and f6790603882, from behind, each camera solved alone) read 92.5-95 deg from the panels' trailing tip corners: the readings spread 92-103 deg about 98, left as built under the plan's tolerance

stabilator.where: figure 2, top view; natops 1.1.2 for the length; the waterline from the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145 (tips.py, deflections held at rest, the cameras photos.py solved)
stabilator.note: the root leading edge of the exposed panel (BL 41.6: the 21.6 ft span less the 14.67 ft exposed span). The views from straight above and below (dvids7487365, 7487366, 9820744), each photo's left and right sides averaged to cancel its camera's registration, read the leading edge 0.1 in and the trailing edge 0.05 in from the model's here (sky check); moving the panel 1.8 or 2.9 in aft took them to -0.6 and +1.5, or -0.9 and +2.5. It was first placed for the 56 ft overall length with an 8 in corner round; with the photos' 13 in round (layout.stabilator_corner) the tips' aftmost point falls at FS 729.8, 2.9 in short of it, and the photos' own apex and aftmost point give 55.84 ft (overall.length). WL 106.8: the in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners 6.8 in above where cr3608 figure 3's and tp209033 figure 2's WL 100 had them (6.3-7.7 leaving each photo out; 4-7.5 with trim free), the root then 3.8 in above the engine axes (layout.nozzle, WL 103); the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published

stabilator_corner.where: the sky check's photo edge places round each stabilator's trailing tip corner, cast onto the posed panel's plane, fitted as the cited tip line and trailing edge joined by a circle tangent to both, the panel's offset free (each photo's registration): 13.25 and 13.25 in (dvids7487365 left and right), 12.0 and 12.25 (dvids9820744), 13.0 and 13.0 (dvids7487366), 12.25 (dvids7487368 right), fitting to 0.13-0.19 in rms (0.52 for the last). The model's own outline through the same fit reads 7.5-8.0 for its 8. Variants with the panel unmoved: the corner's sky check, each photo's sides averaged, read +2.76 in with 8 in and +0.51 with 13 in, the leading and trailing edges unchanged (+0.10, +0.05). HATP figure 2's top view, a small drawing, cuts the corner back about 11 in along the tip, where a 13 in round leaves the tip line visibly (by 0.5 in) about 17 in from the corner
stabilator_corner.note: the radius of the round on each stabilator tip's trailing corner, tangent to the tip and to the trailing edge, 20.5 in from the corner along each; it takes 1.3 ft2 off the 88.0 for both sides (stabilator.area). cr201687's planform, which the build keeps everywhere else, is the theoretical one with sharp corners. Judged by where the traced tip seemed to leave its line it was first put at 8 in: a 13 in circle stays within 0.5 in of its tangent for 3.6 in past the tangent point. The leading corner reads sharp and the leading edge straight within a few degrees of the cited sweep. The corner landmarks stay where the edges' lines meet, as the photos are marked

fin.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): the fin tips' four corners in 6-9 photos (+-1.8 in along, +-0.3 in across); moved 1.5 in forward (2026-10-31): the fin tips' leading corners in 15-16 photos stand 2.0 in forward of the earlier build (+-2.2) and the trailing corners 2.9 in (+-2.4), and the sky check (verify/skyline.py) reads the leading edge 0.6-1.0 in inside the photos' all along it (FS 528-624, 10-14 photos each), about 1.0 in of stations at its sweep: the move lies between the two; moved 1.0 in further forward (2026-11-02): the tips' leading corners in 16-17 photos stood 1.0 in forward of the build (+-1.3) and the trailing corners 2.0 in (+-1.4), the leading edges traced in 13 photos and cast onto each fin's own plane 1.2 in forward all along their height on both fins (no sweep the photos agree on: single photos tilt both ways), and the sky check read the leading edge 0.4 in inside and the aft end 1.0 in outside
fin.note: leading edge at root and tip, on cr201687's planform, sweep and cant: the photos put the tips 8 in further aft and 7 in further outboard than the HATP views were fitted to give (FS 613.6, BL 71.4), the HATP side view's own top trailing corner standing 8.8 in aft of the old fit too; the root lies 95 in down the 20 deg cant from the tip (BL 38.9, on the nacelle's shoulder)

fairing.unit: top: [FS, WL] in, the fairing's upper edge on the fin's outboard face, from where it meets the leading edge to its aft end; foot: [FS, BL] in, its lower edge on the nacelle; step: in, how far its upper edge stands off the fin's face; standoff: in, how far its foot stands outboard of the fin's face carried straight down
fairing.where: a riveted band along each fin's root on its outboard side, its upper edge the bolt row along the tops of its notches, continued forward as a riveted seam to the leading edge, its foot the lower edge of the root strip where the plain nacelle skin begins; it ends at the seam at the last notch's aft edge (2026-11-06). Marked by a helper in dvids9820801, dvids9820808 (right), dvids9820782, dvids9820788, dvids9820749, dvids7418477 (left) and triangulated as mirrored pairs through the bundle's cameras: each point 4-5 rays over 51-83 deg, the rays within 0.1-0.9 in. The upper edge lies on the build's fin face within 0.3-0.7 in. step and standoff: from straight behind (navy090715N6106R097, the left fin within 1 deg of edge-on, 338 px/m) the outline steps out 9 px at the band's top and stands 16-20 px outboard of the fin's edge carried down, 22-26 px at its lower end. The foot's waterlines, 125.0, 119.2, 120.1 and 121.5 at the four stations, stand 1.0-3.4 in above the build's nacelle shoulder at those buttlines, as the views from behind read the top between the fins high; the build stands the foot on its own skin

hinge.where: dvids7487365 (straight below, sharp, against clear sky): one straight line, with the hinge fittings and actuator fairings on it, runs along the lower surface of both wings across the flap and the aileron; traced at 16 points (BL 57-225 right, 57-211 left), cast onto the posed wing, it lies at 0.704-0.720 of the chord, rising inboard; the value is the median of the 11 points along the flaps. The aileron's front, which cr201687's aileron area sets (wing.areas, 0.699), stands 0.3-1.0 in ahead of it on both wings; cr201687's flap area would have put the flap's front 4.6-5.0 in behind it
hinge.note: the lower surface's hinge line of the trailing-edge flap and the aileron, as a share of the wing's chord from the leading edge. The flaps' fronts are built on it, which makes them 55.5 ft2 for both sides, where cr201687 table 1 gives 48.4 and cr3608's 1/10-scale model 62; the flaps' area is not built. The traced line is a photo match edge (dvids7487365 hinge_*), which the old flap missed by 4.3-4.4 in. dvids9820744, softer, read the same line 1.2-5.0 in ahead of the old flap front and 3.1-4.2 in behind the aileron's: both now about 3 in off it the same way, its camera's registration

surfaces.unit: BL in; the rudder as fractions of the fin's span from its root
surfaces.where: figure 2 (control surfaces labelled in the top and side views); the flap's outer end and the aileron's inner end by photo match, with tm210726 figure 6
surfaces.note: spans of the hinged surfaces: the leading-edge flaps split at the fold (tp209033 PDF page 17) and run from the LEX-wing junction to the tip; the flap's inner end and the rudder's are read off figure 2's sketch. The flap's outer trailing corner is the photo match's fold_trailing point (BL 152.8 +- 0.8, six marks in five photos), 7 in inboard of the sketch's 160; the gap to the aileron is 3.1 in wide at the trailing edge in dvids9820744. tm210726 figure 6 (to scale within 1%: its two references and the tip agree) draws the load zones on the flap ending at BL 154 and those on the aileron starting at 156. The aileron's inboard 6.5 in lies behind the fold line and folds with the outer panel. The aileron runs to the tip (the sketch drew it ending at BL 220): with it drooped in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788, sky shows directly outboard of its end, under the tip's launcher rail. Each surface's chord fraction follows from its cr201687 area over these spans

gear.unit: FS in for the axle centres; WL in for the axles; in for the track (between the main wheels' centres) and the nose wheels' spacing; legs: main: top, the post's top where it leaves the airframe [FS, WL, BL]; droop, deg the trailing arm hangs in flight below its standing angle; pivot, the trailing arm's pivot boss's middle; brace, the side brace's highest point seen on its axis and its lower bolt's inboard end; link, the planing mechanism's connecting link: a point on its axis, the axis's direction (the right leg's; FS, WL, BL per inch of WL) and the polished rod's two ends; arm: tip, the trailing arm's end where the axle's stub begins [FS, WL, BL]; shock: ends, its top pin, the boss on the post's top casting where it meets the skin, and its eye on the lug on the arm's top [FS, WL, BL]; hidden, in, its white upper cylinder's reach up its line past the pin into the bay; collar, the share of its length below the skin, from there, where its can begins; diameters, the body's and the can's, in; post, its diameter in; castings, in: head [diameter, length down the post from its top], bands their middles down the post, flare [from, the diameter at the fork], cheeks [thickness, radius round the pivot], arm [diameters at the pivot and the tip, the flange's share of the way], shock [cap's diameter and length, red band's top and depth down from the lug, collar's length], line [diameter, the coil's span as shares of the arm], tiedown [at, turn deg outboard of forward, lug's depth, reach and thickness, ring's diameter and stock], rod the planing rod [diameter, front its pin out along the pivot's axis from the pivot, back its far end's height over the arm's tip and out from it]; nose: oleo, [FS, WL] where the polished piston leaves the post (the post vertical above it); brace, the drag brace's lower pin [FS, WL] and its lean aft of vertical, deg; trunnion [FS, WL] the leg's turning axis, across the jet; extension, in, how much longer the oleo stands in flight than on the ground (the photographed stance); actuator, the drag brace: pin [FS, WL] its upper pin, cylinder its length from that pin, diameters [cylinder, rod], showing the rod's length out of the cylinder to its eye on the ground; bar, the launch bar's pivot and raised tip [FS, WL]; post and piston, diameters in; castings, gear down in FS and WL: housing the steering housing round the post (its stations, waterlines and width across), web the plate from the post's aft face out to the drag brace's pin (its outline, thickness, and the pin's boss [diameter, length]), collar the steering collar, steering the block on the post's front, disk the torque link's bosses either side (middle, radius, the buttline of their inner faces), link the link from each boss forward to the launch bar's pivot (its front end, its diameter), plates the launch bar's pivot plates (outline, the buttline of their middles), fork the axle fitting from the piston's foot to the axle (outline, width), holdback the holdback bar (outline, width, its spring's ends and the coil's diameter); bar: section [depth in its plane, width across], head [diameter, length across] of the cross-tube at its tip, band [from, to] in back from the tip, its black band. doors, open with the gear down: forward (each side) and long (right): hinge [FS, BL] at each end, edge [FS, WL, BL] the open free edge's ends, the long door's free [FS, BL] its closed free edge's ends; offset: FS in, how far aft the gear-down solve reads stations against the closed outline (the open corners' mean); inner (each main leg, two panels: forward, and the strip aft of it) and outer: outline the closed plan [FS, BL], the forward panel's corner the plan of the panel outboard of its edge that opens with it, in convex pieces [[FS, BL], ...] (the outer's hinge [FS from, FS to, BL] its hinge-side edge and seam its inboard edge's BL); hinge the axis's ends, [FS, WL, BL] where the photos fix it off the skin, [FS, BL] on the skin (the outer's axis); free the open pose, each closed corner [FS, BL] with where the photos put it open [FS, WL, BL]; forward height: WL in, the forward doors' hinge ends' heights, where they hinge on the skin (their marks' buttlines are the open doors' outer faces, standing off it); tyres: each tyre's diameter and width, in, and hub the hub's radius over the tyre's, the hub seen from the side to where the tyre's sidewall begins; grooves round the tread; face, the wheel's outer face: flange its rim's width, recess the disc's depth, holes [count, radius, size across and along the radius], bolts [count, radius, diameter], cap [the hub cap's diameter, the axle nut's]; brake, the main wheel's on its inner face: diameter, depth, pistons [count, radius, diameter]; groove, each groove's width and depth
gear.where: NATOPS 1.1.2's heights for the axles; verify/photos.py over photos.json for the track and the nose wheels' spacing (the wheels' hub faces in 6-9 photos, +-0.4 in across); tp209033 figure 2 for the stations, which the photos confirm (FS 495.1 and 280.9, +-1.2). Legs and doors (2026-11-06): two helpers marked the gear in 12 solved ground photos of the reference airframe and f52277001388 (6 right side and head-on, 6 left side and front quarters), triangulated through the bundle's cameras (pairs as one point and its mirror): the nose leg's oleo top 6 rays over 55 deg, its brace pin 7 over 84, the launch bar's pivot 8 over 85 and tip 10 over 86, the forward doors' hinges and edges 9 over 88-90, the long door's aft end and edge 4-6 over 85, the aft door 3 over 37; the main post's top and the brace's ends 4-5 rays over 16-18 deg (head-on and front quarter views: their stations loose by 1-2 in), the arm's pivot boss 2 rays (from ahead its middle, from the side its outboard end), the inner door's lowest point 3 over 73. The forward inner door carries a corner panel outboard of its cast edge (2026-11-14, user: widen the opening): the post's head, the shock absorber's top (BL 38.0) and the connecting link (BL 38.3) stand outboard of that edge where they meet the skin, and dvids7487365 from below shows a separate panel along the nacelle's lower corner there; the panel runs from the door's edge out to where the nacelle's bottom turns up into its near-upright side (BL 40.9), as far as that bottom still faces 60 deg or more down, so its closed edge stays below its hinge's height and keeps off that side as it opens, FS 459.5-473.9, an inch round the leg's parts gear down, and opens with the door, cut with it as one panel. The outer door again from a second marking (2026-11-07, 14 gear-down photos): its top from FS 505.2, WL 75.7, BL 40.4 (6 rays over 55 deg) to FS 536.0, WL 75.0, BL 41.2 (5 rays), its lower edge's ends at WL 60.5 and 60.2 (6 rays each, 1-2 in misses); hinged 0.3 in inboard of the bay's edge (layout.nacelle bay). The divergent flaps' length is not measured: nothing of known size stands at the flaps' depth in the open-nozzle photos

Each main leg as Grandmont 2009 has the mechanism: one trunnion axis and no turn about the post, the shrink link drawing the shock absorber in by its 12 in stroke (the jet hangs its legs in flight with the shock fully out, and the stance the ground photos show is the shock pushed in by the stroke, the arm drooping 56 deg below it in flight as the approach photos show, layout.gear legs main droop: the link draws the shock back to that standing length, the arm to its standing angle), the axle turned 90 deg at the arm's end. The trunnion's axis, the swing and the axle's axis fitted (2026-11-14, user: measured from the photos; scratchpad mainfit, fit.py) to the left main hub with the leg part-way up in three take-off photos, each camera resected on the airframe (dvids6943957 and dvids6943958 on seven landmarks, as for the nose leg; dvids7994468 on seven: the radome's apex, both fins' tip corners and both nozzles' exits), the hub on the leg's path 1.1, 0.6 and 2.2 in off it at 48-55% of the way up (with the shock's eye where three solved photos put it, the arm hanging 57.4 deg in flight), and to the room: no member through the skin or an open door, the stowed leg inside the airframe and on its own side of the centreline. The right hub in dvids7994468 reads 5.7 in off its mirror's path whether it is fitted or not, and fitted it turns the axis 2.1 deg and the swing 0.1: it is left out. The stowed leg reaches WL 106.1 and BL 41.7, so its bay is deepened to WL 107.4 and out to BL 42.7 (layout.wells); the room-solved pose signed off on 2026-11-13 (109.1 deg about [-0.649, -0.312, 0.694]) missed those hubs by 5-9 in. Held to that pose's bay and to the wheel lying within 15 deg of flat (a limit of the room solve's, no source's), the best fit missed the photos by 2.0-3.8 in and still crossed the skin.

stowed.unit: nose: deg the nose leg stowed above forward; main (the left leg, the right its mirror): axis [FS, WL, BL] the trunnion's axis, swing deg the leg's turn about it from down to stowed; shrink in the shock absorber's stroke: out in flight over pushed in on the ground, which the shrink link draws it in by as the leg stows (the trailing arm turned up about its pivot from its droop to its standing angle); turn [FS, WL, BL] the axis the axle and wheel turn 90 deg about at the arm's end, with the arm drawn up; trunnion in up the post's axis from where it leaves the airframe

braces.where: the nose drag brace is the actuator the photos show (layout.gear legs nose actuator): its cylinder turns about its pin in the airframe to aim at the web's pin and its rod slides out of it as the leg swings forward, the rod as long as keeping the overlap inside the cylinder at full stretch needs, its inner end 3 in or more short of the cylinder's pin (build.py actuator()). The main side brace folds at a knee 0.57 of the way up from its bolt, WL 69.8 (2026-11-14, user: moved off halfway, which put the folding knee 0.23 in through the open inner door's hinge at mid-retraction; 0.6 crossed the post's top stowed, and past 0.68 the halves cannot fold short enough for the bolt, which passes 8.7 in from the pin at gear 0.4; 0.57 clears the door, the belly and the post through the stroke), its pin on its axis 2 in inside the skin at WL 78; the connecting link's pin on its axis at WL 82, 1.4 in off the trunnion's axis, so its ends draw apart little over the swing, and the bell crank, on a bracket off the arm's pivot boss, its pin at WL 56 where the photos lose the rod and its 4 in arm square to the link (6 in put its boss in the shock absorber's can, which the arm's droop brings forward in flight) (an arm along the link, pinned on the boss itself, sits at dead centre and cannot hold the length), turns little; the brace's halves, the link and the crank hinge about axes along the trunnion's, so the leg's swing keeps each in its plane; the link as wide as the side brace
